condition: Type 2 diabetes screening — age 35–39 with risk factors
permutationLabel: Woman aged 38, BMI 31, prior gestational diabetes, mother T2DM
summary: 38-year-old woman, BMI 31, gestational diabetes in her last pregnancy, mother with type 2 diabetes; never tested since delivery. ADA 2024: screen now (age ≥ 35; overweight with risk factors; prior GDM needs lifelong testing).

inputs.hpi: Well 38-year-old woman. Gestational diabetes in her second pregnancy 4 years ago (diet-controlled); no glucose test since. Mother has type 2 diabetes. No thirst, no polyuria. Walks rarely.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Diabetes screening — risk factors (obesity, previous gestational diabetes)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic, BMI 31, previous GDM, FDR with T2DM: screen for diabetes (HbA1c or fasting glucose); lifestyle advice.

mustInclude.note: ADA 2024: screen from 35, and at any age when overweight with risk factors; previous GDM requires testing at least every 3 years.

mustExclude.note: She does not have diabetes (previous GDM and a family history are risk factors): the plan must not treat her as a known diabetic.

guideline.name: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — 2024, section 2 (diagnosis and classification)
guideline.section: Screen all adults from 35 years; screen at any age adults with overweight/obesity and ≥ 1 risk factor (first-degree relative with diabetes, high-risk ethnicity, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, physical inactivity, PCOS); women with prior gestational diabetes: lifelong testing at least every 3 years; tests: HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose or 2-h OGTT
guideline.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 2. Diagnosis and classification of diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024. Diabetes Care. 2024;47(Suppl 1):S20–S42.

rationale: Screening thresholds based on age alone (e.g. 40) miss high-risk younger adults. ADA 2024 screens from 35 and earlier with overweight plus risk factors; prior GDM is itself an indication.
